content: The text provided appears to be a list of references from academic and professional publications, primarily focused on workplace mental health, interventions, and related topics. 1. A systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies was conducted, as published in the Scandinavian Journal of Work, Environment & Health, Volume 43, Issue 4, pages 294–306. 2. Yoshimura K, Kawakami N, Tsutsumi A, Inoue A, Kobayashi Y, Takeuchi A, and colleagues performed a cost-benefit analysis of primary prevention programs for mental health in Japanese workplaces. This study was published in the journal Sangyo Eiseigaku Zasshi in 2013, Volume 55, Issue 1, pages 11–24. 3. The International Labour Organization (ILO) published a report on global working conditions, accessible via their website, which was last accessed on August 26, 2022. 4. Houtman I, Jettinghof K, Cedillo L, and the World Health Organization’s Occupational and Environmental Health Team provided guidance on raising awareness of workplace stress in developing countries, offering advice to employers and worker representatives. This document is available on the WHO website and was accessed on August 26, 2022. 5. The WHO outlined international minimum requirements for health protection in the workplace, accessible through their online repository, last accessed on August 26, 2022. 6. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted on December 10, 1948, by the United Nations General Assembly, remains a foundational document for human rights, including workplace rights. It is available on the UN website and was accessed on August 26, 2022. 7. The International Labour Organization’s Convention No. 155, addressing occupational safety and health, was reviewed and accessed on August 26, 2022. 8. Guidelines on mental health at work, as part of the WHO’s global strategy on health, environment, and climate change, emphasize the need for sustainable improvements in well-being through healthy environments. This document was accessed on August 26, 2022. 9. McCulloch P, Rathbone J, and Catchpole K reviewed interventions aimed at improving teamwork and communication among healthcare staff, as published in the British Journal of Surgery in 2011, Volume 98, Issue 4, pages 469–479. 10. Romppanen J and Häggman-Laitila A conducted a quantitative systematic review of interventions designed to enhance nurses’ well-being at work, published in the Journal of Advanced Nursing in 2017, Volume 73, Issue 7, pages 1555–1569. 11. Sakuraya A, Imamura K, Watanabe K, Asai Y, Ando E, Eguchi H, and colleagues systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed randomized controlled trials to identify effective interventions for improving subjective well-being among workers. This study was published in Frontiers in Psychology in 2020, Volume 11, Article 528656. 12. Panagioti M, Panagopoulou E, Bower P, Lewith G, Kontopantelis E, Chew-Graham C, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled interventions aimed at reducing burnout in physicians. This research was published in JAMA Internal Medicine in 2017, Volume 177, Issue 2, pages 195–205. 13. The WHO’s global strategy on human resources for health, titled Workforce 2030, outlines key objectives for improving workforce conditions and was accessed on August 26, 2022. 14. The ILO published guidelines on decent work in public emergency services, which were accessed on August 26, 2022. 15. Alhassan RK, Nketiah-Amponsah E, Spieker N, Kojo Arhinful D, and Rinke de Wit TF assessed the impact of community engagement interventions on health worker motivation and client experiences in Ghana’s primary health facilities. This randomized cluster trial was published in PLoS One in 2016, Volume 11, Issue 7, Article e0158541. 16. Strohmeier H, Scholte WF, and Ager A explored strategies to improve organizational staff support, based on suggestions from humanitarian workers in South Sudan. Their findings were published in the journal Intervention in 2019, Volume 17, Issue 1, pages 40–49. 17. The Seventy-First International Labour Conference reviewed Convention No. 161, focusing on occupational health services, with documentation accessed on August 26, 2022. 18. Zafar N, Rotenberg M, and Rudnick A systematically reviewed workplace accommodations for individuals with mental disorders, as published in the journal Work in 2019, Volume 64, Issue 3, pages 461–475. 19. Bolo C, Sareen J, Patten S, Schmitz N, Currie S, and Wang J examined the relationship between receiving workplace mental health accommodations and the outcomes of mental disorders in employees with depressive and/or anxiety disorders. This study was published in the Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine in 2013, Volume 55, Issue 11, pages 1293–1299. 20. Secker J, Membrey H, Grove B, and Seebohm P contextualized evidence on workplace adjustments in their publication in the Psychiatric Rehabilitation Journal in 2003, Volume 27, Issue 1, page 3. 21. The United Nations’ Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD), adopted by the General Assembly, remains a critical framework for disability rights, including workplace accommodations. It was accessed on August 26, 2022. 22. Chow CM and Cichocki B identified predictors of job accommodations for individuals with psychiatric disabilities, as published in the Rehabilitation Counseling Bulletin in 2016, Volume 59, Issue 3, pages 172–184. 23. Granger B, Baron R, and Robinson S conducted a national survey of job coaches and developers regarding job accommodations for individuals with psychiatric disabilities. Their findings were published in the Journal of Vocational Rehabilitation in 1997, Volume 9, Issue 3, pages 235–251. 24. Chow CM, Cichocki B, and Croft B analyzed the impact of job accommodations on employment outcomes for individuals with psychiatric disabilities, as published in Psychiatric Services in 2014, Volume 65, Issue 9, pages 1126–1132. 25. Wang J, Patten S, Currie S, Sareen J, and Schmitz N investigated perceived needs for and use of workplace accommodations by individuals with depressive and/or anxiety disorders. Their study was published in the Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine in 2011, Volume 53, Issue 11, pages 1268–1272.
